items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: the trumpet section was Sweets Edison, Clark Terry, Nat Adderley

ctx.x: period of working together. Because the circumstances change. I mean you don’t have that regularity because practically you’re always either planning or doing or coming off of a record date when you’re working together. And there’s a great deal of planning together and hanging out together. And when that goes, what you have to recognize is you’re not going to have in most cases, that same kind of closeness. And you have to realize nobody’s mad at anybody necessarily. Sometimes yes, but very often not, it’s just…

Cannonball, who was coming near the end of his Capitol contract and Capitol wasn’t doing anything in jazz at that point. And so Cannonball and I ended up together at Fantasy for what turned out to be the last few years of his life. But in that intervening period between 1964 when Riverside died, and 1973 when we both were together at Fantasy, in that period we remained close personal friends. And we saw a lot of each other, we talked to each other a lot, we shared non-musical things, and that I have to say is…
